paper.title: Prison as a Criminal School: Peer Effects and Criminal Learning behind Bars
paper.journal: The Journal of Law and Economics
paper.code_data_availability: Not stated: the paper prints no data or code availability statement. …

registers.role: outcomes (crime-specific recidivism), criminal histories, incarceration spells, sample frame, co-offending
variables_mentioned: identifiers for both a convicted person and the attached judiciary case

registers.name_in_paper: administrative registers (linked data covering the entire Danish population)
registers.role: controls: individual socioeconomic characteristics and municipality characteristics
variables_mentioned: municipality real gross income per capita

registers.role: facility-specific incarceration spells for the entire prison population (used to construct the peer measures) and the number of local prisons
background statistic: share of immigrants and descendants in the Danish population

linkages: linked data from administrative and police registers covering the entire Danish population over 1991-2010

inmates linked to facility-specific incarceration spells to construct the weighted share of overlapping fellow inmates with a criminal history of offense h (equation 1); peer measures use the entire prison population while the estimation sample is first-time inmates
convicted persons linked to judiciary case identifiers to detect co-offending with previous fellow inmates
individuals linked to their municipality of residence in the year of incarceration

sample.universe: the entire Danish population observed in linked administrative and police registers 1991-2010; the entire Danish prison population is used to construct the peer measures
sample.unit_of_observation: individual (first-time incarcerated young adult); one facility-specific spell per person -- the longest, for the 26 percent who serve across several facilities
selection_rules: incarcerated for the first time at ages 18-21
first incarceration in 1994 or later (incarceration is recorded in the registers only from 1991, and criminal pasts since age 15 must be observable)
first incarceration before the end of 1997 (to avoid the 1999 reform that established sections for strongly negative inmates)
for individuals who serve in several facilities, only the longest facility-specific spell is kept
observation period ends in 2006 (Statistics Denmark began recoding institutions in 2007)

construction_notes: Peer_ijt^h: individual i's days of overlap with fellow inmates with a criminal history of offense h in facility j relative to i's days of overlap with all fellow inmates in facility j, as a weighted sum of daily shares from the date of incarceration to the date of release (equation 1)

seven crime categories: sexual and violent offenses; robbery; vandalism and arson; burglary, theft and fencing; drug-related offenses; offenses against the weapons act; threats against persons and public authorities

excluded categories: other offenses and unknown type of crime; offenses against the tax act and other special acts; offenses against the road traffic act; indecency, procuring and child pornography; document falsification; white-collar crimes
recidivism: at least one new conviction for offense h within 12 months of first release (24 months in Table 6; 36 months in Damm and Gorinas 2016)
Offense_ijt^h equals one if individual i committed an offense of type h before, so any history of crime of type h is accounted for, not only the most recent crime
young peers are fellow inmates under age 26; hardened criminals are fellow inmates with more than 180 days in prison since 1991; own-ethnic-group peers share Western or non-Western origin
ethnic Dane: a person who is neither an immigrant nor a descendant, following Statistics Denmark's definition

predicted recidivism (Table 3) is predicted from individual and municipality characteristics in the year of incarceration and facility fixed effects, excluding municipality characteristics with high multicollinearity
municipality real gross income is about DKK 200,000 (approximately USD 34,000) per capita

claims.statement: Among young adults incarcerated in a Danish prison for the first time, a prior conviction for violent and sexual offenses is positively and significantly correlated with the probability of being convicted of a violent or sexual offense within 12 months after release.

register_source.value: Danish police registers: date of conviction, sentence and type of offense (criminal histories); no DST register code or variable name is stated

definition.value: indicator equal to one if individual i was convicted of offense h (here: a violent or sexual offense) before the first incarceration (criminal history since age 15, constructed from date of conviction, sentence and type of offense), zero otherwise

timing.value: criminal history observed before the first incarceration (since age 15); registers record incarceration from 1991 on

outcome.label: Recidivism with violent and sexual offenses: conviction within 12 months after release

register_source.value: Danish police registers: date of conviction and type of offense (conviction records); no DST register code or variable name is stated

definition.value: indicator equal to one if the individual is convicted of offense h (here: a violent or sexual offense) within 12 months after release from the first incarceration; recidivism is at least one new conviction in that window

timing.value: 12 months after release from the first incarceration (releases 1994-1998; convictions observed to 2006)

units.value: change in the probability of conviction for offense h within 12 months after release (proportion) associated with a prior conviction for that offense; the paper reads .122 as 12 percentage points

estimand.target_population: young adults incarcerated in a Danish prison for the first time between 1994 and 1997 at ages 18-21
estimand.time_horizon: conviction within 12 months after release from the first incarceration

population.description: Young adults incarcerated in a Danish prison for the first time between 1994 and 1997 at ages 18-21 (1994 at age 18; 1995 at ages 18 or 19; 1996 at ages 18-20; 1997 at ages 18-21)
population.period: first incarceration 1994-1997; recidivism and co-offending observed to 2006
subgroups_defined: inmates with a prior conviction for offense h versus inmates with no prior conviction for offense h

peer groups: all-age peers (peer definition 1), peers under age 26 (peer definition 2), peers under 26 of the same ethnic origin, hardened criminals (more than 180 days in prison since 1991), young hardened criminals
population.selection: first-time incarcerated only (to rule out residual peer influence from earlier incarcerations); incarcerated between 1994 and 1997 (registers record incarceration only from 1991, and the 1999 reform created sections for strongly negative inmates); for the 26 percent serving in several facilities only the longest facility-specific spell is kept

identification.source_of_variation: none: a cross-sectional ordinary least squares correlation between criminal history and crime-specific recidivism among first-time incarcerated young adults, used to motivate the study of crime-specific (rather than general) peer effects

key_assumptions.assumption: No causal interpretation is claimed: the estimates describe the correlation between criminal history of offense h and recidivism with offense h, conditional on criminal history of the other six offense types

estimator.value: OLS (linear probability model)

estimation.specification: ordinary least squares regression of an indicator for conviction of offense h within 12 months after release on prior conviction of the same offense and on criminal history of the other six types of offenses; a constant is reported
controls: criminal history of the other six types of offenses (average of off-diagonal coefficients)
estimation.clustering: standard errors clustered at the facility level

source_table.value: Table 2, column 'Violent and Sexual Offenses', row 'Prior offense'

adjustment_set.label: criminal history of the other six types of offenses

ambiguities: The paper describes the Table 2 estimates as correlations ('positively and, in most cases, significantly correlated'), not as causal effects; no causal edge is asserted in graph_fragment.

baseline_mean and outcome_sd are the sample recidivism rate and its overall standard deviation for this crime type from Table 1 (p. 156); the paper prints no control-group mean, because the treatment is a continuous peer-exposure measure.

evidence.how: The table prints a standard error in parentheses under each coefficient and no confidence interval; no interval was derived from it.

definition.value: the weighted average of the share of other inmates with at least one conviction of type h, interacted with an indicator that individual i has a criminal history of offense h (here: a violent or sexual offense). The peer measure Peer_ijt^h is individual i's days of overlap with fellow inmates with a criminal history of offense h in facility j relative to i's days of overlap with all fellow inmates in that facility, cumulated from the date of incarceration to the date of release (equation 1)

register_source.value: Danish police and incarceration registers: date of incarceration, date of release, facility identifier, date of conviction and type of offense; no DST register code or variable name is stated

definition.value: the weighted average of the share of other inmates with at least one conviction of type h, interacted with an indicator that individual i has a criminal history of offense h (here: an offense against the weapons act). The peer measure Peer_ijt^h is individual i's days of overlap with fellow inmates with a criminal history of offense h in facility j relative to i's days of overlap with all fellow inmates in that facility, cumulated from the date of incarceration to the date of release (equation 1)

timing.value: measured during individual i's (longest) facility-specific incarceration spell, 1994-1997, weighted by days of overlap up to the day of release

outcome.label: Predicted recidivism with weapons (within 12 months after release)

register_source.value: Danish police registers: date of conviction and type of offense (conviction records); no DST register code or variable name is stated

definition.value: indicator for whether an individual is convicted of offense h within 12 months after release, predicted using individual and municipality characteristics in the year of incarceration and facility fixed effects; municipality characteristics presenting high multicollinearity are excluded

timing.value: 12 months after release from the first incarceration (releases 1994-1998; convictions observed to 2006)

units.value: change in the predicted probability of conviction for offense h per unit increase in the weighted share of peers with a criminal history of offense h (share on a 0-1 scale)

estimand.target_population: young adults incarcerated for the first time between 1994 and 1997 at ages 18-21 with a prior conviction for weapons
estimand.time_horizon: predicted conviction within 12 months after release

population.description: Young adults incarcerated in a Danish prison for the first time between 1994 and 1997 at ages 18-21 (1994 at age 18; 1995 at ages 18 or 19; 1996 at ages 18-20; 1997 at ages 18-21)
population.period: first incarceration 1994-1997; recidivism and co-offending observed to 2006
subgroups_defined: inmates with a prior conviction for offense h versus inmates with no prior conviction for offense h

peer groups: all-age peers (peer definition 1), peers under age 26 (peer definition 2), peers under 26 of the same ethnic origin, hardened criminals (more than 180 days in prison since 1991), young hardened criminals
population.selection: first-time incarcerated only (to rule out residual peer influence from earlier incarcerations); incarcerated between 1994 and 1997 (registers record incarceration only from 1991, and the 1999 reform created sections for strongly negative inmates); for the 26 percent serving in several facilities only the longest facility-specific spell is kept

identification.source_of_variation: variation in peer composition within facility-by-prior-offense cells

key_assumptions.assumption: The predicted recidivism indicator captures the individual and municipality characteristics relevant for facility assignment, so a correlation with the peer measures indicates selection
key_assumptions.supported_by: the indicator is predicted from individual and municipality characteristics in the year of incarceration and facility fixed effects

threats_discussed: non-random assignment to prison and facility

estimator.value: seemingly unrelated regression (specifications by peer group estimated simultaneously); linear in the interacted peer measures

estimation.clustering: none stated: 'Standard errors are in parentheses' (Table 3 note)

links.pointer_quote: Furthermore, in contrast to Bayer, Hjalmarsson, and Pozen (2009), for violent offenses (including sex crimes and robbery) we do not find evidence of reinforcing peer effects but do find evidence of deterrent peer effects.
By contrast, we find that exposure to offenders in the same specialization deters inmates from recidivism for violent offenses, including sexual offenses and robbery.

claims.statement: Exposure to all-age fellow inmates with a criminal history of violent and sexual offenses does not significantly change the probability that a first-time incarcerated young adult with a prior conviction for that offense is convicted of a violent or sexual offense within 12 months after release (reinforcing peer effect, the paper's β0).

register_source.value: Danish police and incarceration registers: date of incarceration, date of release, facility identifier, date of conviction and type of offense; no DST register code or variable name is stated

definition.value: the weighted average of the share of other inmates with at least one conviction of type h, interacted with an indicator that individual i has a criminal history of offense h (here: a violent or sexual offense). outcome.label: Recidivism with violent and sexual offenses: conviction within 12 months after release

definition.value: indicator equal to one if the individual is convicted of offense h (here: a violent or sexual offense) within 12 months after release from the first incarceration; recidivism is at least one new conviction in that window

timing.value: 12 months after release from the first incarceration (releases 1994-1998; convictions observed to 2006)

units.value: change in the probability of being convicted of offense h per unit increase in the weighted share of peers with a criminal history of offense h (share on a 0-1 scale); the paper reads .043 as 4.3 percentage points and .018 as .018 of a percentage point per percentage-point increase in the share

key_assumptions.assumption: Condition 1: within prisons, the variation in peer composition is uncorrelated with individuals' characteristics (facility-by-prior-offense fixed effects absorb non-random assignment to facilities)

key_assumptions.assumption: Condition 2: the timing of an individual's assignment is orthogonal to peers' characteristics
key_assumptions.supported_by: quarter-of-release fixed effects are included to rule out the existence of any time trend; using a dummy for each quarter of incarceration gives very similar results

key_assumptions.assumption: The effect of average peers' outcome is zero: peer effects operate only through peers' characteristics and not through future peers' outcomes (functional-form restriction used to eliminate the reflection problem)
The estimation sample is restricted to first-time inmates so that no residual exposure to experienced same-crime inmates from earlier incarcerations is omitted from the model
key_assumptions.supported_by: sample construction: young adults incarcerated for the first time between 1994 and 1997

threats_discussed: non-random assignment to prison and to a particular facility (the Danish Prison and Probation Service chooses the facility on the basis of the convict's characteristics and sentence)
facility assignment conditional on observables is not free of selection (Table 3 without facility-by-prior-offense fixed effects)
the reflection problem (Manski 1993)
omitted-variables bias from peers' exposure to experienced same-crime inmates during past incarcerations
only detected recidivism is observed (detected crimes are about 20 percent of committed crimes)
neither the prison section nor the cell composition is registered
robustness_checks: narrower peer definitions: young peers (<26), same-ethnic-origin young peers, hardened criminals (>180 days incarcerated) and young hardened criminals (Table 5)
recidivism within 24 months (Table 6) and within 36 months (reported in Damm and Gorinas 2016)
a dummy for each quarter of incarceration instead of quarter of release
clustering by facility in separate regressions with facility fixed effects
intensive-margin outcomes (number of new convictions up to 36 months, in Damm and Gorinas 2016)
unresolved_confounders: the paper cannot disentangle endogenous effects (giving rise to a social multiplier) from exogenous effects
prison section and cell composition are not registered, so the actual interaction structure is unobserved
descriptive analyses of incarceration length and prison type cannot be given a causal interpretation because of selection issues

definition.value: the weighted average of the share of other inmates under 26 with at least one conviction of type h, interacted with an indicator that individual i has no criminal history of offense h (here: vandalism or arson). The peer measure Peer_ijt^h is individual i's days of overlap with fellow inmates with a criminal history of offense h in facility j relative to i's days of overlap with all fellow inmates in that facility, cumulated from the date of incarceration to the date of release (equation 1)

timing.value: measured during individual i's (longest) facility-specific incarceration spell, 1994-1997, weighted by days of overlap up to the day of release

outcome.label: Recidivism with vandalism and arson: conviction within 12 months after release

register_source.value: Danish police registers: date of conviction and type of offense (conviction records); no DST register code or variable name is stated

definition.value: indicator equal to one if the individual is convicted of offense h (here: vandalism or arson) within 12 months after release from the first incarceration; recidivism is at least one new conviction in that window

timing.value: 12 months after release from the first incarceration (releases 1994-1998; convictions observed to 2006)

units.value: change in the probability of being convicted of offense h per unit increase in the weighted share of peers with a criminal history of offense h (share on a 0-1 scale); the paper reads .043 as 4.3 percentage points and .018 as .018 of a percentage point per percentage-point increase in the share

estimand.target_population: young adults incarcerated in a Danish prison for the first time between 1994 and 1997 at ages 18-21 who have no a prior conviction for vandalism and arson
estimand.time_horizon: conviction for offense h within 12 months after release from the first incarceration

population.description: Young adults incarcerated in a Danish prison for the first time between 1994 and 1997 at ages 18-21 (1994 at age 18; 1995 at ages 18 or 19; 1996 at ages 18-20; 1997 at ages 18-21)
population.period: first incarceration 1994-1997; recidivism and co-offending observed to 2006
subgroups_defined: inmates with a prior conviction for offense h versus inmates with no prior conviction for offense h

peer groups: all-age peers (peer definition 1), peers under age 26 (peer definition 2), peers under 26 of the same ethnic origin, hardened criminals (more than 180 days in prison since 1991), young hardened criminals
population.selection: first-time incarcerated only (to rule out residual peer influence from earlier incarcerations); incarcerated between 1994 and 1997 (registers record incarceration only from 1991, and the 1999 reform created sections for strongly negative inmates); for the 26 percent serving in several facilities only the longest facility-specific spell is kept

identification.source_of_variation: random variation in the duration of overlap in incarceration between a first-time inmate and each fellow inmate with a criminal history of offense h, within facility-by-prior-offense cells (facility, quarter-of-release and facility-by-prior-offense fixed effects included)

facility assignment conditional on observables is not free of selection (Table 3 without facility-by-prior-offense fixed effects)
the reflection problem (Manski 1993)
omitted-variables bias from peers' exposure to experienced same-crime inmates during past incarcerations

a dummy for each quarter of incarceration instead of quarter of release
clustering by facility in separate regressions with facility fixed effects

units.value: change in the probability of being convicted of offense h per unit increase in the weighted share of peers with a criminal history of offense h (share on a 0-1 scale); the paper reads .043 as 4.3 percentage points and .018 as .018 of a percentage point per percentage-point increase in the share
